name: Zhēng Shàngyóu
description: Zhēng Shàngyóu ('Struggling Upstream' / 'Climb to the Top') is a Chinese shedding/climbing game similar to President. 54-card deck (52 + 2 jokers). Play ascending combinations (singles/pairs/triples/sequences/bombs). First out wins. Ranking: 3-A-2-BlackJoker-RedJoker. Bombs beat any combination.

history.origins: Zhēng Shàngyóu (争上游), meaning 'Struggling Upstream', is a Chinese climbing card game whose name is said to recall a literary image of a fish swimming against the current in early spring; some associate it with the Cultural Revolution era. The game exists in several variations and is closely related to Japanese Dai Hin Min, Vietnamese Tien Len, Chinese Big Two, and Western President. It was brought to the UK in 1979 by John McLeod, who learned it from interpreter Zhang Chuansheng during a British Go players' visit to China; in Britain it became known as Pits, referring to the predicament of the losing players. It is particularly popular in Shanghai, Zhejiang, and Jiangsu and forms the basis for many modern climbing games.
timeline: Traditional: Chinese climbing game documented as popular in Shanghai, Zhejiang, Jiangsu; basis for many modern climbing games.
1979: Form described here brought to UK by John McLeod after British Go players' visit to China; introduced in Britain as Pits.
history.cultural: Popular in Shanghai, Zhejiang, Jiangsu; name evokes perseverance; losing players are 'pit dwellers' who give cards to winners in the next hand.
history.evolution: Basis for many modern climbing games; individual and partnership forms (e.g. Sān jiā xĭ, Huŏjiàn) spread regionally.

setup.players: Three to five players (four or more in some descriptions; best with 4–6).
setup.deck: 54 cards: standard 52 plus two distinguishable jokers (Red and Black). Rank order 3 low to A, then 2, Black Joker, Red Joker.
setup.dealing: Dealt singly anticlockwise from dealer until pack is exhausted; depending on player count some players may have one more card.

rules.objective: Be the first to play out all your cards to gain 2 points (or second to gain 1 point) toward a game total of usually 11; the last player left with cards loses the hand and is penalised in the next deal.
rules.gameplay: Lead any combination. Others must play same type, higher rank, or pass. Combinations: single, pair, triple, sequence (3+), full house. Bombs (4+ same rank) beat anything. Pass = out until new trick. Last out loses.

variations.name: Twos in sequences
variations.description: Some allow twos as natural cards in single sequences (e.g. K-A-2 in one suit beats Q-K-A).
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant only changes sequence composition rules; no engine constant overrides documented in sources.

variations.name: Partnership (4 players)
variations.description: Four players in two teams, partners opposite; rules and scoring as individual but partners combine scores.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Partnership is team scoring only; no engine overrides needed for current blueprint.
